key_insight: MuJoCo’s deformable models tracked reference force trends closely but were too stiff and underestimated hysteresis, limiting their accuracy for human–exoskeleton interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Soft-tissue model choice can affect predictions of how exoskeleton attachments transfer assistance to the body.
method: Benchmarked MuJoCo flexcomp Saint Venant–Kirchhoff and Stable Neo-Hookean models against COMSOL’s Yeoh model.
Tested spherical indentation, compression, and thigh compression.
Compared force and strain energy versus indentation depth, hysteresis, and computation time.
evidence_signal: Force correlations were 0.97–0.99; MuJoCo was 2–2.5× faster for spherical indentation, but COMSOL was faster in the other two cases.
watch_item: Possible volumetric locking may explain excess stiffness, while Rayleigh damping did not reproduce viscoelastic hysteresis.
paper_title: Modelling the human-exoskeleton interaction interface - Benchmarking MuJoCo's deformable model
